masters.bio_summary: 宗密為唐代華嚴宗祖師，兼承荷澤禪脈，以華嚴圓教會通禪門修證，於《圓覺》一經用力尤深。

chronology.text: 宗密生於唐德宗建中元年。
宗密卒於唐武宗會昌元年。

masters.name: 宗密

portrait.attribution: Unknown author, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 圭峰宗密傳像

source_classics: cbeta-T-T39n1795-大方廣圓覺修多羅了義經略疏
cbeta-T-T33n1701-金剛般若經疏論纂要卷001
sutras_explained: 大方廣圓覺修多羅了義經
works_commented: 大方廣圓覺修多羅了義經略疏
masters.bio_en: Zongmi combined the Huayan scholarship of Chengguan with Chan training received from Suizhou Daoyuan in the Heze lineage. His Inquiry into the Origin of Humanity compares Buddhist, Confucian and Daoist explanations of human nature. His commentaries on the Sūtra of Perfect Enlightenment connect doctrinal study with meditation.

masters.bio_summary: 德清為晚明高僧，以禪教會通、經疏直解著稱。太虛間今先收其般若、圓覺、楞嚴、楞伽、法華諸疏；《憨山老人夢遊集》可作待入庫之文集與傳記來源。

chronology.text: 德清生於明世宗嘉靖二十五年。
德清卒於明熹宗天啟三年。

masters.name: 德清

portrait.attribution: Anonymous ancient woodblock artist, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 憨山德清木刻傳像

sutras_explained: 大方廣圓覺修多羅了義經
masters.bio_en: Hanshan Deqing wrote commentaries on the Diamond, Śūraṅgama, Laṅkāvatāra and other sūtras while advocating both Chan and Pure Land practice. His collected writings, the Dream-Roaming Collection, preserve sermons, letters and autobiographical material from his career in late Ming China.

masters.bio_summary: 太虛為近代漢傳佛教改革與判教大師，倡人生佛教、八宗平等，以五乘共法、三乘共法、大乘不共法判攝佛法。

chronology.text: 倡教理革命、教制革命、教產革命三大革命。

masters.name: 太虛

portrait.attribution: Unknown author, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 太虛大師，一九二九年倫敦影像

cbeta-太虛-第一編-佛法之分宗判教
cbeta-太虛-第五編-能斷金剛般若波羅密多經釋

般若波羅密多心經講義
masters.bio_en: Taixu advocated reforms of Buddhist institutions, monastic education and religious practice in modern China. He founded the Wuchang Buddhist Institute in 1922 and promoted Buddhism for human life. His teaching classifications sought to accommodate the eight Chinese Buddhist schools within a common framework.

masters.bio_summary: 天台宗實際開宗祖師，立止觀與判教之綱。
masters.name: 智顗

portrait.attribution: Unknown author, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 天台智者大師傳像

masters.bio_en: Zhiyi (538–597) studied under Huisi before teaching in the southern capital and at Mount Tiantai. He organized Buddhist scriptures around the Lotus Sūtra and developed a system of meditation joining calming and insight. His lectures on the Lotus Sūtra and the Great Calming and Contemplation were recorded and edited by his disciple Guanding. These works became the central texts of the Tiantai tradition.

masters.bio_summary: 天台前脈重鎮，傳智顗以法華三昧之學。
masters.name: 慧思

portrait.attribution: Miuki via Wikimedia Commons; source described as 佛光山舊圖
portrait.caption: 南嶽慧思傳像

masters.bio_en: Huisi taught meditation on the Lotus Sūtra and trained Zhiyi, whose work shaped the Tiantai tradition. He later settled at Mount Nanyue; his writings include the Meaning of the Lotus Sūtra's Practice of Ease and Bliss.

masters.bio_summary: 智顗弟子，整理天台三大部，傳述其教觀。
masters.name: 灌頂

portrait.attribution: Miuki via Wikimedia Commons; source described as 佛光山舊圖
portrait.caption: 章安灌頂傳像

masters.bio_en: Guanding attended Zhiyi's lectures and preserved his teaching in edited records. These include the Great Calming and Contemplation and the two principal Tiantai commentaries on the Lotus Sūtra.

masters.bio_summary: 華嚴宗祖師，立五教十宗與法界緣起之義。
masters.name: 法藏

portrait.attribution: Unknown 13th-century artist, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 賢首法藏傳像

masters.bio_en: Fazang (643–712) was born in Chang'an to a family of Sogdian ancestry and studied under Zhiyan. Supported by Empress Wu, he taught the Avataṃsaka Sūtra and participated in Buddhist translation projects. His writings explain the interdependence of all phenomena and classify Buddhist teachings into five categories. The Huayan tradition counts him as its third patriarch, and his Treatise on the Golden Lion illustrates its account of the relation between principle and phenomena.

masters.bio_summary: 華嚴清涼國師，弘揚華嚴圓教，為宗密所承義學重鎮。
masters.name: 澄觀

portrait.attribution: Artists of the Nara to Edo periods, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 清涼澄觀傳像

masters.bio_en: Chengguan wrote a major commentary and subcommentary on the eighty-fascicle Avataṃsaka Sūtra. His account of the relations between principle and phenomena shaped later Huayan interpretation, including the writings of his student Zongmi.

masters.bio_summary: 三論宗大師，闡龍樹中觀，明二諦與破邪顯正。
masters.name: 吉藏

portrait.attribution: Artists of the Nara to Edo periods, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 嘉祥吉藏傳像

masters.bio_en: Jizang (549–623) studied under Falang at Xinghuang Monastery in Jiankang. He later taught at Jiaxiang Monastery in Kuaiji and at monasteries in Chang'an, becoming a leading exponent of the Sanlun tradition. His commentaries on the three Madhyamaka treatises and his Meaning of the Two Truths reject attachment to fixed philosophical positions. He also wrote on the Lotus, Vimalakīrti and Nirvāṇa sūtras.

masters.bio_summary: 姚秦譯師，譯《中論》《法華》《金剛》等，為漢地般若與三論之源。
masters.name: 鳩摩羅什

portrait.attribution: 唐吉訶德的侍從 via Wikimedia Commons; based on 1909 三教源流搜神大全
portrait.caption: 鳩摩羅什傳像

masters.bio_en: Kumārajīva (344–413) grew up in Kucha and studied Buddhist teachings in Central Asia and Kashmir. After years of detention in Liangzhou, he reached Chang'an in 401, where the Later Qin ruler Yao Xing supported his translation work. Working with Chinese monks, including Sengzhao, he produced influential versions of the Lotus Sūtra, Diamond Sūtra and Vimalakīrti Sūtra. His translations of Madhyamaka treatises supplied the textual basis for the later Sanlun tradition.

masters.bio_summary: 羅什門下高足，以般若中觀會通玄學語境。
masters.name: 僧肇
masters.bio_en: Sengzhao worked with Kumārajīva's translation community in Chang'an. Essays collected in the Zhao lun discuss emptiness, wisdom and the relation between movement and stillness, drawing on Prajñāpāramitā and Madhyamaka teachings.

masters.bio_summary: 唐代大譯師，傳瑜伽行派法相唯識之學。
masters.name: 玄奘

portrait.attribution: Unknown author, Tokyo National Museum / ColBase, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 玄奘三藏傳像

masters.bio_en: Xuanzang (602–664) travelled through Central Asia to India to resolve questions about Buddhist doctrine. At Nālandā he studied Yogācāra under Śīlabhadra, returning to Chang'an in 645 with Sanskrit manuscripts. With imperial support, he led translation teams at monasteries including Daci'en and translated major works on consciousness, Abhidharma and the perfection of wisdom. His Great Tang Record of the Western Regions, compiled with Bianji, describes the lands he visited. His disciple Kuiji developed the commentarial tradition later known as Faxiang.

masters.bio_summary: 玄奘弟子，法相唯識宗祖師之一。
masters.name: 窺基

portrait.attribution: Unknown author, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 慈恩窺基傳像

masters.bio_en: Kuiji (632–682) studied under Xuanzang and worked in his translation circle in Chang'an. Based at Daci'en Monastery, he became known as the master of Ci'en. His commentary on the Cheng weishi lun explains the synthesis of Indian Yogācāra interpretations transmitted by Xuanzang. He also wrote on Buddhist logic and the Lotus Sūtra, and later Faxiang lineages regarded him as a founding teacher.

masters.bio_summary: 瑜伽行派要師，唯識諸論之重鎮。
masters.name: 世親

portrait.attribution: Unknown author, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 世親傳像

masters.bio_en: Vasubandhu wrote the Abhidharmakośa and its commentary, examining the categories and arguments of Buddhist scholasticism. Works associated with his Yogācāra teaching include the Twenty Verses and Thirty Verses on consciousness, both extensively studied in East Asia.

masters.bio_summary: 禪宗傳統以達摩為西天第二十八祖、東土初祖，象徵直指心源之法脈。
masters.name: 達摩

portrait.attribution: Tsukioka Yoshitoshi, 1887, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 月岡芳年所繪達摩像

masters.bio_en: Early Chinese sources associate Bodhidharma with meditation and teachings related to the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra. Later Chan genealogies make him the first Chinese patriarch and the teacher of Huike. The treatise on the Two Entrances and Four Practices is attributed to him, although much of his biography belongs to later legend.

masters.bio_summary: 禪宗二祖，傳統法脈承達摩。
masters.name: 慧可

portrait.attribution: Attributed to Shi Ke, via Wikimedia Commons / Tokyo National Museum tradition
portrait.caption: 二祖慧可調心圖

masters.bio_en: Huike is recognized in Chan tradition as the second Chinese patriarch. Traditional lineage accounts present him as Bodhidharma's successor.

masters.bio_summary: 禪宗六祖，《六祖壇經》所記頓教法門之核心人物。
masters.name: 慧能

portrait.attribution: Unknown photographer/source, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 六祖慧能肉身影像

masters.bio_en: Huineng (638–713) is remembered as a Chan teacher in southern China, associated with Caoxi and Baolin Monastery. Later lineage accounts identify him as Hongren's successor and the sixth Chinese patriarch. The Platform Sūtra presents teachings in his name on sudden awakening and the inseparability of meditation and wisdom. Shenhui promoted his lineage in the eighth century, helping establish its later prominence. Much of his biography survives in retrospective religious narratives, whose details cannot all be treated as historical fact.

masters.bio_summary: 荷澤禪要師，宗密所承禪脈由此上接慧能。
masters.name: 神會

portrait.attribution: Unknown author; source: Shaolin Temple Website, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 荷澤神會傳繪

masters.bio_en: Heze Shenhui publicly championed Huineng's lineage and criticized the claims of teachers associated with Shenxiu. His campaign helped establish the distinction between Southern and Northern Chan. Zongmi later inherited the Heze tradition and discussed its teachings in his accounts of Chan.

masters.bio_summary: 禪宗傳統三祖，東土六祖譜系中承慧可、下接道信。
masters.name: 僧璨

portrait.attribution: Unknown author, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 三祖僧璨傳像

masters.bio_en: Sengcan is recognized in Chan tradition as the third Chinese patriarch. Traditional genealogies place him between Huike and Daoxin.

masters.bio_summary: 禪宗傳統四祖，東土六祖譜系中承僧璨、下接弘忍。
masters.name: 道信

portrait.attribution: User Thinman10 / Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 四祖道信傳像

masters.bio_en: Daoxin led a monastic community at Mount Shuangfeng in Huangmei and taught Hongren. Chan genealogies count him as the fourth Chinese patriarch, between Sengcan and Hongren.

masters.bio_summary: 禪宗傳統五祖，東土六祖譜系中承道信，後開慧能、神秀諸脈。
masters.name: 弘忍
masters.bio_en: Hongren taught at the East Mountain community in Huangmei, following Daoxin. Later sources identify both Shenxiu and Huineng as his disciples and place him fifth in the Chinese Chan patriarchal succession.

masters.bio_summary: 唐代禪門要師，傳統譜系中與弘忍門下北宗禪脈相關。
masters.name: 神秀
masters.bio_en: Shenxiu trained in Hongren's community and later taught at Yuquan Monastery. Invited to the imperial court under Empress Wu, he became a prominent Chan teacher. His lineage was later labelled Northern Chan by its critics.

masters.bio_summary: 六祖後南嶽一脈之要師，傳統上為一花五葉中臨濟、溈仰諸脈之前承。
masters.name: 懷讓
masters.bio_en: Nanyue Huairang was a Chan teacher placed in Huineng's lineage by traditional accounts. The Linji and Guiyang lineages trace their ancestry through him.

masters.bio_summary: 六祖後青原一脈之要師，傳統上為一花五葉中曹洞、雲門、法眼諸脈之前承。
masters.name: 行思
masters.bio_en: Qingyuan Xingsi was a Chan teacher placed in Huineng's lineage by traditional accounts. The Caodong, Yunmen and Fayan traditions trace their ancestry through his branch.

masters.bio_summary: 南嶽一脈要師，為一花五葉中臨濟、溈仰諸脈之前承。
masters.name: 道一
masters.bio_en: Mazu Daoyi taught in Hongzhou in present-day Jiangxi, where his community became a major centre of Tang Chan. Traditional accounts identify Nanyue Huairang as his teacher and Baizhang Huaihai and Nanquan Puyuan among his disciples.

masters.bio_summary: 青原一脈要師，傳統上為曹洞、雲門、法眼諸脈之前承。
masters.name: 希遷
masters.bio_en: Shitou Xiqian was a Tang Chan teacher associated with the Qingyuan lineage. Later genealogies trace the Caodong, Yunmen and Fayan traditions through him.

masters.bio_summary: 馬祖門下要師，臨濟、溈仰二脈之近前承。
masters.name: 懷海
masters.bio_en: Baizhang Huaihai taught in Jiangxi after studying with Mazu Daoyi. His disciples included Huangbo Xiyun and Weishan Lingyou, through whom later genealogies trace the Linji and Guiyang traditions. Later monastic rules invoke his authority, although a complete original code by him does not survive.

masters.bio_summary: 百丈門下要師，傳統上為臨濟義玄之前承。
masters.name: 希運
masters.bio_en: Huangbo Xiyun belonged to Baizhang Huaihai's lineage and taught Linji Yixuan according to Chan transmission records. The official Pei Xiu collected teachings attributed to him in the Essentials of Mind Transmission and the Wanling Record.

masters.bio_summary: 臨濟宗宗祖，為一花五葉之一。
masters.name: 義玄
masters.bio_en: Linji Yixuan taught at Linji Monastery in Zhenzhou after training under Huangbo Xiyun, according to Chan records. Dialogues and sermons attributed to him were later compiled in the Record of Linji. His name became that of the Linji tradition, one of the five houses of Chan.

masters.bio_summary: 百丈門下要師，與仰山慧寂共成溈仰宗脈。
masters.name: 靈祐
masters.bio_en: Weishan Lingyou was a Chan teacher in Baizhang Huaihai's lineage. Together with his disciple Yangshan Huiji, he is associated with the formation of the Guiyang tradition.

masters.bio_summary: 溈山門下要師，與溈山靈祐共成溈仰宗脈。
masters.name: 慧寂
masters.bio_en: Yangshan Huiji was a disciple of Weishan Lingyou. The Guiyang tradition of Chan takes its name from the two teachers' mountain names.

masters.bio_summary: 曹洞宗宗祖之一，青原石頭一脈之後承。
masters.name: 良价
masters.bio_en: Dongshan Liangjie studied with Yunyan Tansheng and taught at Mount Dongshan in Jiangxi. Later Caodong lineages trace their ancestry through his community, which included Caoshan Benji and Yunju Daoying.

masters.bio_summary: 洞山門下要師，與洞山良价共成曹洞宗脈。
masters.name: 本寂
masters.bio_en: Caoshan Benji was a disciple of Dongshan Liangjie. He is associated with the formation of the Caodong tradition of Chan.

masters.bio_summary: 雲門宗宗祖，為一花五葉之一，屬青原石頭一脈後承。
masters.name: 文偃
masters.bio_en: Yunmen Wenyan trained under Xuefeng Yicun and later taught at Mount Yunmen in Guangdong. His recorded sayings became important sources for Chan case collections. The Yunmen tradition takes its name from his teaching centre.

masters.bio_summary: 法眼宗宗祖，為一花五葉之一，屬青原石頭一脈後承。
masters.name: 文益
masters.bio_en: Fayan Wenyi studied with Luohan Guichen and later taught at Qingliang Monastery in Jinling under Southern Tang patronage. His disciples included Tiantai Deshao. Later genealogies made him the founder of the Fayan house of Chan.

masters.bio_summary: 廬山結社念佛，為漢地淨土傳統重要先驅。
masters.name: 慧遠
masters.bio_en: Huiyuan studied under Dao'an before establishing a monastic community at Donglin Monastery on Mount Lu. He corresponded with Kumārajīva on doctrinal questions. His community's practice of recollecting Amitābha led later Pure Land genealogies to count him as an early patriarch.

masters.bio_summary: 唐代淨土宗大師，弘持名念佛與彌陀本願。
masters.name: 善導

portrait.attribution: Muromachi-period artist, Otani University Museum, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 善導大師像

masters.bio_en: Shandao (613–681) studied Pure Land practice under Daochuo at Xuanzhong Monastery before teaching in Chang'an. His Commentary on the Contemplation Sūtra explains rebirth in Amitābha's Pure Land in terms of the Buddha's vows and the practices of ordinary people. He gave particular weight to reciting Amitābha's name while also teaching contemplation and liturgical practice. His writings became major sources for Chinese and Japanese Pure Land traditions.

masters.bio_summary: 永明延壽會通禪淨，後世視為禪淨雙修之要脈。
masters.name: 延壽
masters.bio_en: Yongming Yanshou studied under Tiantai Deshao and became abbot of Yongming Monastery in Hangzhou. His hundred-fascicle Record of the Source Mirror draws together scriptural quotations and doctrinal discussion. Later Chan and Pure Land traditions both claimed his legacy.

masters.bio_summary: 晚明高僧，弘淨土念佛，與德清等同為晚明佛教重鎮。
masters.name: 祩宏

portrait.attribution: 黃存吾繪，《青林高會圖》局部，via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 《青林高會圖》所見蓮池祩宏像

masters.bio_en: Lianchi Zhuhong rebuilt Yunqi Monastery near Hangzhou and promoted monastic discipline and the recitation of Amitābha's name. His commentary on the Amitābha Sūtra and his rules and exhortations addressed both monastic and lay practice.

masters.bio_summary: 南山律宗祖師，整理四分律學與僧史。
masters.name: 道宣

portrait.attribution: Kamakura-period artist, Nara National Museum / eMuseum, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 南山道宣像

works_authored: 四分律刪繁補闕行事鈔
masters.bio_en: Daoxuan (596–667) studied monastic discipline under Zhishou and spent much of his career around Chang'an and Mount Zhongnan. His commentaries on the Dharmaguptaka Vinaya established the basis of the Nanshan Vinaya tradition. He briefly assisted Xuanzang's translation work and served as abbot of Ximing Monastery. His Further Biographies of Eminent Monks and other historical compilations preserve extensive records of Chinese Buddhist institutions and practitioners.

masters.bio_summary: 唐代律師，東渡日本傳戒，為東亞律學重要人物。
masters.name: 鑑真

portrait.attribution: Ogawa Seiyou, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 鑑真和上像

masters.bio_en: Jianzhen travelled from Yangzhou to Japan in 753 after several failed crossings. He conducted ordinations at Tōdaiji and established Tōshōdaiji in Nara. His teaching helped institutionalize the Dharmaguptaka Vinaya in Japan.

masters.bio_summary: 唐代譯師與求法僧，記印度與南海佛教制度，譯律部經論。
masters.name: 義淨

portrait.attribution: User:L joo, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 義淨三藏想像像

masters.bio_en: Yijing sailed to India via Śrīvijaya and studied at Nālandā before returning to China in 695. His Record of Buddhist Practices Sent Home from the Southern Sea describes monastic life in India and Southeast Asia. His translations include substantial portions of the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya.

masters.bio_summary: 開元三大士之一，傳胎藏密法，譯《大日經》。
masters.name: 善無畏

portrait.attribution: Anonymous, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 善無畏三藏傳像

masters.bio_en: Śubhakarasiṃha (637–735) was an Indian monk who arrived in Chang'an in 716. Working with the Chinese monk Yixing, he translated the Mahāvairocana Sūtra and explained its ritual and contemplative practices. Yixing recorded his explanations in a commentary that became central to East Asian esoteric Buddhism. The teachings associated with this scripture underlie the Womb Realm tradition. He is remembered with Vajrabodhi and Amoghavajra as one of the Three Great Masters of the Kaiyuan era.

masters.bio_summary: 開元三大士之一，傳金剛界密法。
masters.name: 金剛智

portrait.attribution: Anonymous, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 金剛智三藏傳像

masters.bio_en: Vajrabodhi (671–741) was an Indian monk who travelled by sea through Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia before reaching China in 720. In Chang'an he translated esoteric scriptures and taught initiation and ritual practices associated with the Vajraśekhara cycle and the Vajra Realm. His disciple Amoghavajra assisted him and continued this work after his death. Along with Śubhakarasiṃha and Amoghavajra, he is known as one of the Three Great Masters of the Kaiyuan era.

masters.bio_summary: 開元三大士之一，唐密譯經與儀軌傳承之重鎮。
masters.name: 不空

portrait.attribution: Unknown author, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 不空三藏傳像

masters.bio_en: Born in 705, Amoghavajra became Vajrabodhi's disciple while young and accompanied him to Tang China. After his teacher's death, he travelled to Sri Lanka to study and collect esoteric scriptures. Returning to Chang'an, he based his translation work at Daxingshan Monastery and served the courts of Xuanzong, Suzong and Daizong. He is remembered with Vajrabodhi and Śubhakarasiṃha as one of the Three Great Masters of the Kaiyuan era. More than one hundred translated works are attributed to him, including scriptures and ritual manuals of esoteric Buddhism. He died in 774.

masters.bio_summary: 唐長安青龍寺東塔院阿闍梨，金胎兩部付法於空海。
masters.name: 惠果
masters.bio_en: Huiguo (746–805) was a disciple of Amoghavajra and an esoteric Buddhist teacher at Qinglong Monastery in Chang'an. He taught both the Vajra Realm and Womb Realm systems of initiation and ritual. In 805 he transmitted both systems to the visiting Japanese monk Kūkai. Kūkai's account of their meeting and his subsequent teaching in Japan made Huiguo a central figure in the Shingon lineage.

masters.bio_summary: 讚岐人，804 年隨遣唐使入唐，805 年於長安青龍寺盡受惠果兩部大法，806 年歸國開真言宗（東密），816 年開高野山；奉淳和天皇敕撰《十住心論》十卷，立十住心判教，攝顯密於一綱。
masters.name: 空海
works_authored: 大毘盧遮那成佛經疏文次第
masters.bio_en: Kūkai (774–835), born in Sanuki, travelled to Tang China in 804. At Qinglong Monastery in Chang'an he received the Vajra Realm and Womb Realm transmissions from Huiguo in 805, returning to Japan the following year. He established the Shingon tradition and obtained permission to found a monastic centre at Mount Kōya in 816. He also directed esoteric Buddhist activities at Tōji in Kyoto. His Treatise on the Ten Stages of Mind sets out a classification of Buddhist and non-Buddhist teachings.

masters.bio_summary: 唐代僧人，參與《大日經疏》傳承，亦以曆算聞名。
masters.name: 一行
masters.bio_en: Yixing (683–727), born Zhang Sui, was a Tang monk, astronomer and mathematician. He worked with Śubhakarasiṃha on the Chinese translation of the Mahāvairocana Sūtra and recorded explanations that formed its principal Chinese commentary. At the imperial court he conducted astronomical research and organized observations used in calendrical reform. His work led to the Dayan calendar, which was adopted after his death.

masters.bio_summary: 近代佛教復興重要居士，創金陵刻經處，啟太虛等近代佛教教育之脈。
masters.name: 楊仁山
masters.bio_en: Yang Wenhui founded the Jinling Buddhist Press in Nanjing in 1866 to recover and circulate Buddhist texts. He also established the Jetavana Hermitage school, attended by Taixu and other figures in the modern Buddhist revival.

masters.bio_summary: 太虛弟子，譯介藏傳佛教經論。
masters.name: 法尊
masters.bio_en: Fazun studied Tibetan Buddhism and worked in Taixu's educational network. His Chinese translations include Tsongkhapa's Great Treatise on the Stages of the Path to Enlightenment. He also taught at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute.

masters.bio_summary: 承太虛人間佛教之願，而以中觀與佛教史研究重建現代佛學。
masters.name: 印順
masters.bio_en: Yinshun developed historical studies of Indian and Chinese Buddhism while participating in the reform movement associated with Taixu. His works include The Way to Buddhahood and a study of the history of Chinese Chan. His account of Buddhism for the human realm influenced later Taiwanese Buddhist communities.

masters.bio_summary: 近代佛教教育人物，與太虛法脈相關，台灣佛學教育早期重鎮。
masters.name: 慈航
masters.bio_en: Cihang participated in Taixu's Buddhist educational movement and taught in Southeast Asia before settling in Taiwan in 1948. He established a Buddhist institute there and supported the education of young monastics.

masters.bio_summary: 晚明高僧，與蓮池、憨山、蕅益並列晚明佛教要脈。
masters.name: 真可

portrait.attribution: Unknown author, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 紫柏真可傳像

masters.bio_en: Zibai Zhenke travelled widely during the late Ming and worked to restore Buddhist monasteries. He supported the publication of the Jiaxing Buddhist canon, whose bound volumes made canonical texts more convenient to circulate.

masters.bio_summary: 晚明清初高僧，融通天台、淨土與戒學。
masters.name: 智旭
masters.bio_en: Ouyi Zhixu wrote on Tiantai doctrine, Pure Land practice and monastic discipline during the late Ming and early Qing. His works include Essential Explanation of the Amitābha Sūtra and a critical catalogue of the Buddhist canon.

masters.bio_summary: 唐代天台中興祖師，闡發智顗教觀，使天台義學於中唐復振。
masters.name: 湛然
masters.bio_en: Zhanran wrote detailed commentaries on Zhiyi's meditation and scriptural teaching. His Diamond Scalpel argues that Buddha-nature extends even to insentient things. His work helped renew Tiantai scholarship in the Tang.

masters.bio_summary: 華嚴宗初祖傳統所宗，後世以其法界觀門為華嚴觀行之源。
masters.name: 杜順
masters.bio_en: Dushun is regarded in Huayan tradition as its first patriarch. Later accounts associate him with contemplative approaches to the dharma realm.

masters.bio_summary: 華嚴二祖傳統所宗，承杜順而啟法藏，闡華嚴義學。
masters.name: 智儼
masters.bio_en: Zhiyan was a Tang Buddhist scholar regarded as the second Huayan patriarch. Traditional accounts connect him with Dushun and identify him as a teacher of Fazang.

masters.bio_summary: 瑜伽行派重要論師，與世親並為唯識義學之源。
masters.name: 無著

portrait.attribution: Unkei sculpture; photo by Shihachi Fujimoto, via Wikimedia Commons
portrait.caption: 無著像

masters.bio_en: Asaṅga is associated with the formation of Indian Yogācāra and with treatises on the bodhisattva path. Works attributed to him include the Compendium of the Great Vehicle and the Abhidharmasamuccaya. His relationship with Vasubandhu is central to later accounts of the Yogācāra lineage.

masters.bio_summary: 唐代唯識學僧，與玄奘譯場及解深密、唯識義學相關。
masters.name: 圓測
masters.bio_en: Yuance was a Buddhist scholar active in Tang China and associated with Xuanzang's translation circle. He wrote on Yogācāra and the Saṃdhinirmocana Sutra.

masters.bio_summary: 淨土宗前期重要祖師，闡他力往生之義，為道綽、善導淨土教之先聲。
masters.name: 曇鸞
masters.bio_en: Tanluan wrote a commentary on the Treatise on Rebirth attributed to Vasubandhu. It explains Pure Land practice through Amitābha's vows and the dedication of merit. Later teachers, including Daochuo and Shandao, developed themes found in this work.

masters.bio_summary: 淨土宗祖師，承曇鸞淨土義，開善導持名念佛教法之前脈。
masters.name: 道綽
masters.bio_en: Daochuo taught at Xuanzhong Monastery, where Tanluan's legacy influenced his turn to Pure Land practice. His Collection on Peace and Bliss distinguishes the path of sages from the Pure Land path. Shandao studied under him before teaching in Chang'an.

masters.bio_summary: 摩訶迦葉為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第1祖。
masters.name: 摩訶迦葉
masters.bio_en: Mahākāśyapa is remembered in Buddhist sources as a prominent disciple of the Buddha. Chan tradition places him first in its lineage of Indian patriarchs.

masters.bio_summary: 阿難為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第2祖。
masters.name: 阿難
masters.bio_en: Ānanda is remembered in Buddhist sources as a disciple and attendant of the Buddha. Chan tradition places him second in its lineage of Indian patriarchs.

masters.bio_summary: 商那和修為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第3祖。
masters.name: 商那和修
masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Shangnahexiu as Indian patriarch number 3, following Anan. They name Youpojuduo as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 優婆鞠多為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第4祖。
masters.name: 優婆鞠多
masters.bio_en: Upagupta is a Buddhist teacher known from traditions about King Aśoka. Chan genealogies place him fourth in the lineage of Indian patriarchs.

masters.bio_summary: 提多迦為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第5祖。
masters.name: 提多迦

portrait.attribution: 守一編，《佛祖統系道影》，瑪瑙經房善書局，1880；Wikimedia Commons extraction。
portrait.caption: 提多迦傳統道影

masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Tiduojia as Indian patriarch number 5, following Youpojuduo. They name Mizhejia as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 彌遮迦為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第6祖。
masters.name: 彌遮迦

portrait.attribution: 守一編，《佛祖統系道影》，瑪瑙經房善書局，1880；Wikimedia Commons extraction。
portrait.caption: 彌遮迦傳統道影

masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Mizhejia as Indian patriarch number 6, following Tiduojia. They name Posumi as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 婆須蜜為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第7祖。
masters.name: 婆須蜜

portrait.attribution: 守一編，《佛祖統系道影》，瑪瑙經房善書局，1880；Wikimedia Commons extraction。
portrait.caption: 婆須蜜傳統道影

masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Posumi as Indian patriarch number 7, following Mizhejia. They name Fotuonanti as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 佛陀難提為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第8祖。
masters.name: 佛陀難提

portrait.attribution: 守一編，《佛祖統系道影》，瑪瑙經房善書局，1880；Wikimedia Commons extraction。
portrait.caption: 佛陀難提傳統道影

masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Fotuonanti as Indian patriarch number 8, following Posumi. They name Futuomiduo as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 伏馱蜜多為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第9祖。
masters.name: 伏馱蜜多

portrait.attribution: 守一編，《佛祖統系道影》，瑪瑙經房善書局，1880；Wikimedia Commons extraction。
portrait.caption: 伏馱蜜多傳統道影

masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Futuomiduo as Indian patriarch number 9, following Fotuonanti. They name Xie Zunzhe as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 脅尊者為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第10祖。
masters.name: 脅尊者

portrait.attribution: 守一編，《佛祖統系道影》，瑪瑙經房善書局，1880；Wikimedia Commons extraction。
portrait.caption: 脅尊者傳統道影

masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Xie Zunzhe as Indian patriarch number 10, following Futuomiduo. They name Funayeshe as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 富那耶舍為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第11祖。
masters.name: 富那耶舍
masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Funayeshe as Indian patriarch number 11, following Xie Zunzhe. They name Maming as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 馬鳴為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第12祖。
masters.name: 馬鳴
masters.bio_en: Aśvaghoṣa composed Sanskrit Buddhist poetry, including the Buddhacarita on the Buddha's life and the Saundarananda on Nanda's path to liberation. Later Chan genealogies count him as the twelfth Indian patriarch.

masters.bio_summary: 迦毗摩羅為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第13祖。
masters.name: 迦毗摩羅

portrait.attribution: 守一編，《佛祖統系道影》，瑪瑙經房善書局，1880；Wikimedia Commons extraction。
portrait.caption: 迦毗摩羅傳統道影

masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Jiapimoluo as Indian patriarch number 13, following Maming. They name Longshu as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 龍樹為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第14祖。
masters.name: 龍樹
masters.bio_en: Nāgārjuna's Fundamental Verses on the Middle Way analyzes causation, identity and other categories through the teaching of emptiness. His writings became central to Madhyamaka in India and to Sanlun interpretation in China. Later Chan genealogies place him fourteenth among the Indian patriarchs.

masters.bio_summary: 迦那提婆為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第15祖。
masters.name: 迦那提婆
masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Jianatipo as Indian patriarch number 15, following Longshu. They name Luohouluoduo as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 羅侯羅多為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第16祖。
masters.name: 羅侯羅多

portrait.attribution: 守一編，《佛祖統系道影》，瑪瑙經房善書局，1880；Wikimedia Commons extraction。
portrait.caption: 羅侯羅多傳統道影

masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Luohouluoduo as Indian patriarch number 16, following Jianatipo. They name Sengqienanti as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 僧伽難提為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第17祖。
masters.name: 僧伽難提

portrait.attribution: 守一編，《佛祖統系道影》，瑪瑙經房善書局，1880；Wikimedia Commons extraction。
portrait.caption: 僧伽難提傳統道影

masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Sengqienanti as Indian patriarch number 17, following Luohouluoduo. They name Qieyesheduo as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 伽耶舍多為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第18祖。
masters.name: 伽耶舍多

portrait.attribution: 守一編，《佛祖統系道影》，瑪瑙經房善書局，1880；Wikimedia Commons extraction。
portrait.caption: 伽耶舍多傳統道影

masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Qieyesheduo as Indian patriarch number 18, following Sengqienanti. They name Jiumoluoduo as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 鳩摩羅多為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第19祖。
masters.name: 鳩摩羅多
masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Jiumoluoduo as Indian patriarch number 19, following Qieyesheduo. They name Sheyeduo as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 闍夜多為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第20祖。
masters.name: 闍夜多
masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Sheyeduo as Indian patriarch number 20, following Jiumoluoduo. They name Poxiupantou as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 摩拏羅為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第22祖。
masters.name: 摩拏羅
masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Monaluo as Indian patriarch number 22, following Poxiupantou. They name Helena as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 鶴勒那為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第23祖。
masters.name: 鶴勒那
masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Helena as Indian patriarch number 23, following Monaluo. They name Shizi as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 師子尊者為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第24祖。
masters.name: 師子尊者
masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Shizi as Indian patriarch number 24, following Helena. They name Poshesiduo as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 婆舍斯多為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第25祖。
masters.name: 婆舍斯多
masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Poshesiduo as Indian patriarch number 25, following Shizi. They name Burumiduo as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 不如蜜多為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第26祖。
masters.name: 不如蜜多
masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Burumiduo as Indian patriarch number 26, following Poshesiduo. They name Boreduoluo as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 般若多羅為禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第27祖。
masters.name: 般若多羅
masters.bio_en: Traditional Chan genealogies count Boreduoluo as Indian patriarch number 27, following Burumiduo. They name Putidamo as his successor; these lineage accounts do not provide an independently established biography.

masters.bio_summary: 宋代臨濟宗師，黃龍、楊岐二派之上承關鍵人物；v1 先作五家七宗譜系骨架。
masters.name: 楚圓
masters.bio_en: Shishuang Chuyuan studied under Fenyang Shanzhao in the Linji lineage. Huanglong Huinan and Yangqi Fanghui were among his disciples, and their teaching communities became the two principal Song branches of Linji Chan.

masters.bio_summary: 宋代臨濟宗黃龍派祖師；v1 先列為五家七宗之一支。
masters.name: 慧南
masters.bio_en: Huanglong Huinan studied with Shishuang Chuyuan and later taught at Mount Huanglong in Jiangxi. The Huanglong branch of Linji Chan traces its name and lineage to his teaching community.

masters.bio_summary: 宋代臨濟宗楊岐派祖師；v1 先列為五家七宗之一支。
masters.name: 方會
masters.bio_en: Yangqi Fanghui trained under Shishuang Chuyuan and taught at Mount Yangqi in Jiangxi. His lineage, transmitted through Baiyun Shouduan and later teachers, became a major branch of Linji Chan.

masters.bio_summary: 禪宗西天二十八祖傳統譜系第二十一祖。燈錄謂其一食不臥、六時禮佛，受闍夜多付法，傳摩拏羅。與唯識論師世親同名而別為一人，譜系之說不作史學定論。
masters.name: 婆修盤頭
masters.bio_en: Poxiupantou is listed as the twenty-first Indian patriarch in traditional Chan genealogies. This catalogue treats that lineage figure separately from the Yogācāra philosopher Vasubandhu; the historical identification remains uncertain.

masters.bio_summary: 石頭希遷法嗣，住澧州藥山。道吾圓智、雲巖曇晟、船子德誠皆出其門，曹洞一系由此下開。
masters.name: 惟儼
masters.bio_en: Yaoshan Weiyan was a Chan teacher traditionally placed in Shitou Xiqian's lineage. His disciples included Yunyan Tansheng, through whom later genealogies trace the Caodong tradition.

masters.bio_summary: 初參百丈懷海二十年未契，後嗣藥山惟儼，住潭州雲巖。傳洞山良价，為曹洞宗之所自出。
masters.name: 曇晟
masters.bio_en: Yunyan Tansheng was a Chan teacher associated with Yaoshan Weiyan. Traditional accounts identify him as the teacher of Dongshan Liangjie, a founding figure of Caodong Chan.

masters.bio_summary: 先參徑山國一、馬祖道一，終嗣石頭希遷，住荊州天皇寺。下傳龍潭崇信，雲門、法眼二宗皆出此脈。
masters.name: 道悟
masters.bio_en: Tianhuang Daowu was a Chan teacher based at Tianhuang Monastery in Jingzhou. Traditional accounts place him in Shitou Xiqian's lineage and identify Longtan Chongxin as his successor.

masters.bio_summary: 天皇道悟法嗣，結庵澧州龍潭。德山宣鑒於其處吹燭而悟，焚《青龍疏鈔》。
masters.name: 崇信
masters.bio_en: Longtan Chongxin was a Chan teacher associated with Longtan in Lizhou. Traditional accounts place him after Tianhuang Daowu and identify him as the teacher of Deshan Xuanjian.

masters.bio_summary: 初精《金剛經》，號周金剛；參龍潭崇信悟道，住朗州德山，以棒接人，世稱德山棒。門下出雪峯義存、巖頭全豁。
masters.name: 宣鑒
masters.bio_en: Deshan Xuanjian was a Chan teacher traditionally associated with Longtan Chongxin. His teaching community included Xuefeng Yicun and Yantou Quanhuo.

masters.bio_summary: 德山宣鑒法嗣，開福州雪峯山，常眾千五百。雲門文偃、玄沙師備、長慶慧稜、保福從展皆出其門，雲門、法眼二宗並由此分。
masters.name: 義存
masters.bio_en: Xuefeng Yicun was a Chan teacher active at Mount Xuefeng near Fuzhou. Traditional genealogies place him in Deshan Xuanjian's lineage and trace the Yunmen and Fayan traditions through his community.

masters.bio_summary: 本以漁為業，年三十出家，行頭陀，號備頭陀。嗣雪峯義存，住福州玄沙。傳羅漢桂琛，法眼宗之所自出。
masters.name: 師備
masters.bio_en: Xuansha Shibei was a Chan teacher associated with Xuefeng Yicun and active in Fuzhou. Traditional accounts identify Luohan Guichen as his successor in a lineage leading to Fayan Chan.

masters.bio_summary: 嗣玄沙師備，住漳州羅漢院，又稱地藏桂琛。以「不知最親切」一語開法眼文益之悟。
masters.name: 桂琛
masters.bio_en: Luohan Guichen, also known as Dizang Guichen, was a Chan teacher associated with Xuansha Shibei. Traditional accounts identify him as the teacher of Fayan Wenyi.

masters.bio_summary: 嗣法眼文益，入天台山尋智者遺蹟，興其道場；吳越王錢俶尊為國師。傳永明延壽，法眼宗盛於吳越。
masters.name: 德韶
masters.bio_en: Tiantai Deshao was a Chan teacher in Fayan Wenyi's lineage who worked in the Wuyue kingdom. He was associated with Buddhist institutions at Mount Tiantai and taught Yongming Yanshou.

masters.bio_summary: 嗣臨濟義玄，住魏府興化寺。傳南院慧顒，臨濟一宗賴以相續。
masters.name: 存獎
masters.bio_en: Xinghua Cunjiang was a Chan teacher traditionally identified as a successor of Linji Yixuan. He taught at Xinghua Monastery and transmitted the lineage to Nanyuan Huiyong.

masters.bio_summary: 嗣興化存獎，住汝州寶應院，世稱南院。燈錄目錄但題寶應和尚。傳風穴延沼。
masters.name: 慧顒
masters.bio_en: Nanyuan Huiyong was a Chan teacher associated with Baoying Monastery in Ruzhou. Traditional genealogies place him between Xinghua Cunjiang and Fengxue Yanzhao in the Linji lineage.

masters.bio_summary: 初習天台止觀，後參南院慧顒得法，住汝州風穴寺。五代之際臨濟幾絕，賴其振起；傳首山省念。
masters.name: 延沼
masters.bio_en: Fengxue Yanzhao was a Chan teacher at Fengxue Monastery in Ruzhou. Traditional accounts place him after Nanyuan Huiyong and identify Shoushan Shengnian as his successor in the Linji lineage.

masters.bio_summary: 常誦《法華》，人稱念法華。嗣風穴延沼，開法汝州首山。傳汾陽善昭。
masters.name: 省念
masters.bio_en: Shoushan Shengnian was a Chan teacher active at Mount Shoushan in Ruzhou. Traditional genealogies place him after Fengxue Yanzhao and identify Fenyang Shanzhao as his successor.

masters.bio_summary: 遍參諸方，後嗣首山省念，住汾州太子院。作頌古百則，開宋代頌古之風；門下石霜楚圓出黃龍、楊岐二派。
masters.name: 善昭
masters.bio_en: Fenyang Shanzhao was a Chan teacher in the Linji tradition and a successor of Shoushan Shengnian. His verses on earlier Chan cases contributed to the development of Song Buddhist literary practice.

masters.bio_summary: 遇荷澤神會授以心訣，後結茅太行山。燈錄列為神會法嗣，傳荊南惟忠。
masters.name: 法如
masters.bio_en: Cizhou Faru appears in Chan transmission records as a disciple of Heze Shenhui. These accounts associate him with the Taihang Mountains and identify Jingnan Weizhong as his successor.

masters.bio_summary: 又名南印。燈錄列磁州法如下，住荊南；傳遂州道圓。
masters.name: 惟忠
masters.bio_en: Jingnan Weizhong, also called Nanyin, appears in Chan transmission records in Cizhou Faru's lineage. The records associate him with Jingnan and identify Suizhou Daoyuan as his successor.

masters.bio_summary: 嗣荊南惟忠，住遂州大雲寺。宗密赴舉途經遂州，聞其說法，隨之出家，即圭峯宗密之本師。
masters.name: 道圓
masters.bio_en: Suizhou Daoyuan was a Chan teacher associated with Dayun Monastery in Suizhou. Traditional accounts place him in Jingnan Weizhong's lineage and identify him as the teacher under whom Zongmi became a monk.

masters.bio_summary: 嗣馬祖道一，於池州南泉山築禪院，三十年不下山。「平常心是道」、斬貓諸則出焉。傳趙州從諗、長沙景岑。
masters.name: 普願
masters.bio_en: Nanquan Puyuan was a Chan teacher in Mazu Daoyi's lineage, active at Mount Nanquan in Chizhou. Later Chan literature preserves dialogues associated with him, and traditional accounts identify Zhaozhou Congshen among his disciples.

masters.bio_summary: 嗣南泉普願，八十猶行腳，後住趙州觀音院四十年。「喫茶去」「狗子無佛性」諸則，為後世公案之宗。
masters.name: 從諗
masters.bio_en: Zhaozhou Congshen was a Chan teacher in Nanquan Puyuan's lineage, later based at Guanyin Monastery in Zhaozhou. Dialogues attributed to him became widely used cases in later Chan literature.
